character: Hockenheim's 3.74km National Circuit — a shortened version of the Grand Prix layout that keeps the fast Nordkurve, the long Parabolika back straight and the tight Spitzkehre hairpin, then runs the technical Motodrom stadium section in front of the grandstands. Traction out of the slow corners and hard braking into the hairpin define the lap.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockenheimring (National Circuit, 3.736km, 15 turns; 2002 Tilke redesign) ; https://www.racingcircuits.info/europe/germany/hockenheimring.html — Nordkurve / Parabolika / Spitzkehre / Motodrom naming
notes: Forza labels this variant 'National Circuit' (3.69km). Wikipedia lists the National Circuit at 3.736km with 15 turns — the shortened GP layout without the full stadium loop. Corner names are the well-documented modern-circuit names; the National variant's exact turn-by-turn numbering was not cleanly sourced, so entries render under their own names rather than turn numbers.

corners.name: Nordkurve
corners.type: medium-fast right-hander off the front straight (Turn 1)
corners.technique: Firm braking, late apex, get the car rotated for a clean exit
corners.trap: Running wide compromises the run to the following section

corners.name: Einfahrt Parabolika
corners.type: tight right that turns the lap back on itself onto the Parabolika
corners.technique: Brake hard, patient entry, prioritise exit drive onto the long straight
corners.trap: Over-slowing or a poor exit costs speed down the entire Parabolika

corners.name: Parabolika
corners.type: long, gently sweeping left that acts as the back straight
corners.technique: Flat out — keep the car settled and hold a tidy line into the Spitzkehre braking zone
corners.trap: Drifting off line late unsettles the car for the heavy braking that follows

corners.name: Spitzkehre
corners.type: very tight 160-degree hairpin at the end of the Parabolika
corners.technique: Hard, late braking from very high speed (around 280 to 50 km/h), patient throttle on exit
corners.trap: Locking the front from the huge approach speed, or getting on power too early and spinning the wheels

corners.name: Sachskurve
corners.type: fast right leading into the Motodrom stadium section
corners.technique: Commit through the corner and make a smooth transition into the technical stadium sequence
corners.trap: Over-driving the entry and compromising the stadium section that follows

corners.name: Motodrom
corners.type: tight, technical stadium section in front of the grandstands (final corners)
corners.technique: Patient, precise inputs through the tightening sequence; a clean exit onto the front straight is critical
corners.trap: A compromised exit here costs time down the entire front straight
